plan.about: The quarterly review plan the F1 Finance Audit Machine follows for the invented HANGS Construction Services LLC. A review is inquiry and analytical procedures, not an audit: nothing is confirmed with third parties, vouched or sampled. The runner reads its rates, thresholds and comparisons from here; the Review Files system shows it. Every name and figure is invented.
plan.period: Quarter ended September 30, 2026 (the first quarter of fiscal 2027)
plan.reader: The bonding company and the lender read these quarterly statements.

materiality.label: Interim review materiality
materiality.why: A contractor's quarterly income swings with job estimates, so revenue is the steadier benchmark the bonding company watches. These are the FY2026 audit plan's rates applied to the quarter's revenue: the interim review's own materiality, not the year's. The engagement partner sets the final amounts.

comparisons: The same quarter last year (July to September 2025)
analytics.rule: A line is investigated when its change is more than half of materiality and more than 10%. Gross margin is investigated when it moves more than one percentage point.

expectations.how: Recomputed job by job from the contract schedule: costs to date over estimated total costs, times the total contract
Each job's quarter revenue at the margin its June 30 estimate expected
The Q3 payroll ledger, the same ledger the payroll returns were prepared from
Each loan's balance, rate and days in the quarter, on the loan agreement's actual/360 basis
5% of every active job's billings to date

plan.inquiries: Twelve written questions to the controller: each investigated fluctuation, plus accounting changes, related parties, subsequent events, claims, covenants, fraud and going concern.

procedures.what: Agree the trial balance's three columns, tie the interim statements to it, and propose materiality and the threshold for investigating a fluctuation.
Compare the income statement with the prior quarter, the same quarter last year and the budget, and the balance sheet with June 30 and a year earlier. Flag every line over the threshold.
Record the controller's written answer to every flagged fluctuation and to the standard review inquiries, and look for related parties.
Recompute earned revenue on every job, tie it and the job costs to the books, explain the billing swing and retainage, and test each job's margin against its June 30 estimate.
Tie wages and accrued wages to the payroll ledger, set an expectation for interest from the loans, and recompute the loan covenants as the agreement defines them.
Set what was found against materiality, list the open items and write the workpapers and the draft review memo. The CPA concludes and decides what is reported.

answers.question: Why is contract revenue higher than last quarter and than the budget?
answers.answer: Pier 9 Tech Center was at full framing crews all quarter and Alder Point moved into interior work. Rainier Commons and Weller Street started in the quarter. Revenue is the job schedule: costs to date against estimated total costs on every job. Subcontractor costs rose with the work, so payables and the retainage we hold back from subcontractors rose too.

answers.question: Why did the job schedule move from billings ahead of revenue at June 30 to revenue ahead of billings at September 30?
answers.answer: Mostly Alder Point. Its estimate now includes pending change order PCO-14 for the MRI suite shielding redesign, $640,000, which we priced and submitted on August 28. The owner’s architect has reviewed the pricing and we expect the owner to sign it in November. We cannot bill it until it is signed.

answers.question: Why is the gross margin lower than last quarter and the budget?
answers.answer: Tideflats Cold Storage. In August we found cracks in tilt-up wall panels and 14 panels are being recast, and our insulated metal panel supplier raised its price 9%. We revised the estimate at September 30 from $16,284,000 to $17,480,000. We have a backcharge claim against the panel precaster that we have not recorded. The job is still profitable. No other job’s estimate changed by more than a rounding amount.

answers.question: Why did accrued wages nearly double since June 30?
answers.answer: The September 30 accrual covers wages earned September 14 to 30, paid on October 2 and October 16. At June 30 the accrual covered only June 22 to 30.

answers.question: How is interest on the Cinderbrook loans recorded?
answers.answer: Interest on both Cinderbrook loans is accrued monthly. The bank debits it on the first of the following month.

answers.question: Why is cash lower and the line of credit higher than at June 30?
answers.answer: We drew $1,200,000 on the line on August 14 to pay subcontractors on Pier 9 Tech Center while two owner payments were late. Receivables are up because September billings were larger and Juniper Ridge Partners’ September billing was still open at quarter end.

answers.question: Do you have any transactions with related parties?
answers.answer: The Juniper Ridge Business Park job (J-2625), nine flex buildings, is built for Juniper Ridge Partners LLC, a commercial developer with the same owners as HGC, building flex industrial units on land it owns. It is billed on the same terms as other owners.

answers.question: Did any accounting policy or estimate method change in the quarter?
answers.answer: No. We use the same cost-to-cost method and the same change order policy as at June 30.

answers.question: Has anything happened since September 30 that could affect the statements?
answers.answer: On October 9 we drew another $500,000 on the line. Lakeside Clinic started in October and was first billed on October 30.

answers.question: Are there any claims, disputes or lawsuits by or against the company?
answers.answer: Only our backcharge claim against the Tideflats panel precaster. No owner has made a claim against us.

answers.question: Was the company in compliance with the Cinderbrook covenants at September 30?
answers.answer: Yes. Our compliance certificate goes to the bank by November 14, 2026.
